title: Basic composition standardization preserves eldercare providers’ household-work, travel, and social-time profile
source_unit: ATUS respondent age 15+ with one selected diary day, final and 160 replicate weights, standardized within supported age-band x sex x labor-force-status cells

denominator.unit: respondents in 30 supported age-band x sex x labor-force-status cells; provider n=1,319, nonprovider n=6,316

household_work_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

care_for_people_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

work_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

travel_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

socializing_communicating_difference_min.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

secondary_childcare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean secondary-childcare minutes per diary day

eldercare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean eldercare minutes per diary day

observations.method: Aggregate ATUS activity records by TUCASEID, define provider status from any eldercare-roster record, and standardize both groups to the pooled final-weight distribution of supported age bands (15-24, 25-44, 45-64, 65+) crossed with TESEX and TELFS. Differences and standard errors use the 160-replicate ATUS formula.
observations.uncertainty: Replicate-weight uncertainty is propagated through the standardized difference. Only cells represented by both provider statuses are retained. This is an adjusted descriptive association, not a causal effect.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare-roster providers versus respondents without a roster record, standardized across age, sex, and labor-force-status cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: The residual profile may reflect health, family structure, recipient need, occupation, schedule control, diary timing, or other unmeasured selection; the paid-work contrast is imprecise relative to the household-work and social-time contrasts.

denominator.unit: respondents in 33 supported age-band x sex x labor-force-status cells; provider n=1,016, nonprovider n=5,110

household_work_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

travel_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

socializing_communicating_difference_min.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

secondary_childcare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean secondary-childcare minutes per diary day

eldercare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean eldercare minutes per diary day

observations.method: Same standardization and replicate-weight procedure as the 2024 observation, applied to the 2025 ATUS files.
observations.uncertainty: Replicate-weight uncertainty; 2024 and 2025 are separate annual samples and not the same respondents. Supported-cell overlap is required.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare-roster providers versus respondents without a roster record, standardized across age, sex, and labor-force-status cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: A residual time profile is not evidence of care-caused displacement; health, family, recipient, occupation, schedule, and diary-timing differences remain open, and the paid-work contrast is imprecise.

boundary: Basic age, sex, and labor-force-status standardization does not create a causal care exposure. The contrast remains a one-day annual comparison; it does not measure dated care onset, health, family structure, recipient need, schedule control, employer accommodation, recovery, trust, political action, or causal displacement.
